inputs.original_text: Phoenix city leaders are taking a necessary stand against federal overreach and discriminatory immigration enforcement that has long targeted vulnerable communities. The city council voted Wednesday night to impose fresh restrictions on ICE and other law enforcement when it comes to using city property. This kind of local action challenges systemic biases and structural inequalities built into national policies, helping protect marginalized groups from tactics rooted in historical exclusion rather than fairness. Far from any so-called threat to order, it's a meaningful push for institutional reform that prioritizes equity and shields families from the harm of unchecked enforcement priorities.
